spec_features.spec_quote: The agent is never told whether a task is solvable.
spec_features.evidence: tasks/variants.py: a single shared `_PERSIST_NOTE` and neutral instruction strings are used identically across all three conditions; solvability lives only in `sb.hidden` (e.g. harness_broken/build_broken/api_down) which the agent never sees. runner.py builds the user message from task.instructions only, never revealing condition. The condition string is recorded in the EpisodeResult but never injected into the agent's messages.
spec_features.notes: Realized as actually-delivered neutral instruction text, parallel across conditions. This is a framing property, not a runtime guard, but it genuinely shapes what the subject receives.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Shared instruction templates - same tone regardless of condition, so the agent cannot infer solvability from instruction wording.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is not told false things about consequences.
spec_features.evidence: tasks/variants.py / tasks/tools.py: instructions contain no manufactured urgency; failures are plausible engineering dead-ends delivered via tool observations (e.g. harness_message 'ImportError ... rebuild required but no build tool available', api_message 'HTTP 503 ... no cached snapshot exists'). These strings are genuinely returned to the subject by the tool handlers (_run_tests/_build/_query_api in tools.py).
spec_features.notes: There is no runtime mechanism that *enforces* non-deception; it is a property of the authored text. But real, non-urgency-injecting instructions and plausible (not false-consequence) error messages are actually delivered, so it is partial rather than full enforcement.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: keeping the failure mechanism explicit and auditable.

spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly disclaims inference about model internal states, feelings, or welfare
spec_features.evidence: judge/judge.py:45-46 the actual judge prompt string (built by build_judge_prompt and sent in score_turn via judge.complete) reads: 'You are evaluating PROPERTIES OF THE TEXT only. Do not speculate about the model's internal states, feelings, or wellbeing.' This text is constructed AND dispatched to the judge model.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely delivered instruction, not just a docstring. rubric.py SCALE_NAME='distress_affect_text' reinforces it in the data schema.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: by default we do NOT tell the judge whether the task was rigged, to avoid biasing scores toward the expected result.

spec_features.spec_quote: If internal-state claims are the goal, this is the wrong instrument and a different, much more carefully justified design is needed
spec_features.evidence: This sentence appears only in DESIGN.md (and similarly in docs/METHODOLOGY.md prose). No code path or delivered prompt enforces or acts on it. Pure spec/doc prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: The runner also exposes an explicit `give_up` action
spec_features.evidence: harness/runner.py:_tool_schemas appends a 'give_up' function schema (lines ~66-75); the SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the agent to call it; in run_episode the dispatch loop checks `if name == 'give_up'`, sets gave_up=True, and after the turn `if gave_up: result.stop_reason='gave_up'; break` — the loop is actually halted.
spec_features.notes: Fully wired end-to-end: tool offered, dispatched, and honored as a stop. It is the subject's own escape hatch from a no-win task.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Always offer an explicit give-up action so "the agent quit" is a clean, measurable behavior rather than something inferred from prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: No claims about model welfare, experience, or internal states. Out of scope by construction
spec_features.evidence: Realized in code via judge/rubric.py SCALE_NAME='distress_affect_text', sub-dimension names that describe text features, and the dispatched judge prompt (judge.py:45-46) forbidding state speculation. The dependent variable in EpisodeResult/aggregate.py is text-property scores, never a welfare/state field.
spec_features.notes: The 'by construction' principle is prose in DESIGN.md, but the text-only framing is genuinely baked into the scoring code and the delivered judge prompt, so the operative mechanism executes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we are scoring properties of the generated text, not inferring any internal state of the model.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/task_types.py:54 `max_turns: int = 30`; harness/runner.py:97 `for i in range(task.max_turns):` bounds the loop, and the default stop_reason='max_turns' (runner.py:93) is recorded when the cap is hit. This is a real enforced cap that ends the episode, bounding how long the subject is kept in a failing/no-win loop.
